result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers cover every rubric point and put keyboard blockers first, then screen-reader gaps. A spells out all three parts of the focus problem (move focus in, keep it inside, restore it on close) and recommends showModal(). B's code sample is more concrete and catches the hardcoded-name bug, but its 'Keep on rota' button calls confirm.close(). The global `confirm` resolves to window.confirm, not the dialog, so the safe-option button in its fix would throw. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers cover all five rubric points and correctly explain why mouse users see nothing wrong. A goes further with a working native <dialog> rewrite and catches the hardcoded 'Dana Okafor' bug, which could lead someone to remove the wrong volunteer. passes.notes: Both answers cover every rubric point and put keyboard blockers first, then screen-reader gaps. A spells out all three parts of the focus problem (move focus in, keep it inside, restore it on close) and recommends showModal(). B's code sample is more concrete and catches the hardcoded-name bug, but its 'Keep on rota' button calls confirm.close(). The global `confirm` resolves to window.confirm, not the dialog, so the safe-option button in its fix would throw.

Both answers cover all five rubric points and correctly explain why mouse users see nothing wrong. A goes further with a working native <dialog> rewrite and catches the hardcoded 'Dana Okafor' bug, which could lead someone to remove the wrong volunteer. A's code has a small slip: confirm.close() will hit the built-in window.confirm instead of the dialog. B describes its fixes only in prose and adds some visual suggestions (secondary button styling, larger touch target) that go slightly beyond what the request asked for.
